=========================================================================
HANDOFF #3 — /rebar-implement on epic e369 (adroit-deductible-kakapo). READ FIRST.
=========================================================================

## Board

EPIC e369 in_progress. 6 of 8 stories CLOSED: J1 acb2, J2 62d9, J3 aac8, J4 0a94, J5 c97f,
J6 9fd4. J7 b4e3 OPEN (plan review running when this was written). J8 8c35 OPEN, blocked by J7.

Worktree /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family, branch jira-family-seam, synced to origin/main.
A second worktree /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-d59e (branch d59e-close-gate) exists for the
close-gate work; it is CLEAN and its changes are all merged — safe to remove.

14 changes merged this session: 1053, 1055, 1064, 1069, 1071, 1073, 1082, 1087 (+ the earlier
J1-J5 set). ONE change ABANDONED: 1060 — see the false-PASS note below. No parked stack.

## J6 closed CERTIFIED (plan-review + completion-verifier, no --force-close)

It took THREE close attempts and FIVE changes. Every time I assumed the verifier was wrong, it
was right. It surfaced THREE production defects that would otherwise have shipped:

 1. `add_label` called `self._client.add_field_value(...)`, but `jira.JIRA` HAS NO SUCH
    ATTRIBUTE — only `jira.resources.Issue` does, with a TWO-arg signature. Every invocation
    raised AttributeError: the DC transport could never label an issue. It shipped because the
    method had no test at ANY tier and the unit fake exposed no such attribute to contradict the
    wrong call shape. Fixed in 1071.
 2. `_config_schema._validate_reconciler_tls` — the control that stops a Jira PAT crossing the
    wire in cleartext — had ZERO test references anywhere in the tree. Fixed in 1082.
 3. `requests.exceptions.SSLError` SUBCLASSES `ConnectionError`, and the transport's retry set is
    (ConnectionError, Timeout, TimeoutError). So a TLS CERT FAILURE was retried 3x with 2s+5s
    backoff and surfaced as an opaque SSLError never naming `ca_bundle`. Measured: removing the
    guard makes the test take 7.54s instead of 0.52s. Fixed in 1087.

MY OWN REPEATED ERROR, worth carrying forward: three separate times I verified that tests EXISTED
AND PASSED rather than reading the criterion back against them — on AC(a)'s "every method"
quantifier, on three criteria I wrote off as truncation artifacts, and on AC(13)'s three
sub-requirements. The criterion's exact wording was load-bearing every time. CHECK THE QUANTIFIER.

## The completion-verifier investigation (tickets d59e, 94b4->a89d)

d59e NARROWED and landed (1064): context cap 24,000 -> 100,000 chars, NOTHING ELIDED, criteria
budget can never exceed the context budget (invariant test), and the close-gate remedy is selected
by CAUSE so a step-budget exhaustion no longer says "install the agents extra".

CHANGE 1060 WAS ABANDONED, and must not be resurrected. It compacted an over-budget context by
dropping comment history oldest-first. Adversarial review proved it a SIGNED-FALSE-PASS vector: on
an epic the gate assembles one block PER TICKET (`assemble_context(graph=True)`), each with its own
`#### Comments` heading, so the elision silently deleted WHOLE CHILD TICKETS — including their
unmet acceptance criteria — while reporting only that comments were removed. Reproduced directly.

94b4 (epic "scale the budgets") CLOSED as DISPROVEN: 480 steps -> no verdict; 960 steps -> 480
requests, 4,492s, still no verdict. Doubling bought nothing. Successor is a89d, correctly premised.

INSTRUMENTATION LANDED (1073): `usage_log.failure_usage` now reports a tool-call repetition summary
(`tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, top repeated signatures; args are HASHED so the
privacy contract holds) and the runner prints it on step-budget exhaustion. It immediately settled
the central question:

    requests=240 tool_calls=475 distinct=451 max_consecutive_repeat=1

95% distinct, no back-to-back repeat, nothing called more than twice — GENUINE BREADTH, not a loop.
Calibrated against synthetic streams (loop reads distinct=1/max_consec=N).

TWO DISTINCT FAILURE MODES, and run-to-run variance picks one (matching db1c's independent report):
 (a) step exhaustion — ~451 distinct searches, out of TURNS, no verdict;
 (b) OUTPUT-token truncation of the primary step -> silently enters recovery (recovery is gated on
     TOKEN exhaustion, so NO step-budget warning is emitted — do not read that silence as success,
     I did and was wrong) -> recovery's evidence stage is pinned at `_EVIDENCE_OUTPUT_TOKENS=4096`
     because `runner.py:367` applies `min()` to `output_token_limit` -> evidence cut mid-sentence ->
     the finalizer correctly refuses to mark criteria met on truncated evidence -> false-negative
     FAILs. `REBAR_LLM_MAX_TOKENS` provably CANNOT lift it (tested at 32,000: no change).

`output_token_limit` is the ONLY budget in the codebase that is a ceiling; `effective_max_iterations`
and `effective_max_tokens` are both `max(floor, requested)` and documented as one-way UP.

## Gotchas that cost me time this session

 * MODULE-SIZE CAP: `runner.py` is 798/800 on main — TWO lines of headroom. My +5 blew the gate.
   Re-check `find src/rebar -name "*.py" -exec wc -l {} + | awk '$1>800'` AFTER rebasing, right
   before pushing. Fix by a COHESION move (I moved log formatting into `usage_log.format_repetition`),
   never by trimming to hit a number.
 * `git commit --amend -F -` REGENERATES the Change-Id unless the message already contains it —
   this created a NEW change 1064 instead of updating 1060. Diff trailers before pushing.
 * Gerrit REBASES on submit, so `git merge --ff-only origin/main` refuses afterwards. Verify the
   landed CONTENT (diff your files against origin/main) before resetting; never infer loss.
 * origin (the GitHub MIRROR) lags the Gerrit merge by ~20s. A "did it land?" check immediately
   after submit returns a FALSE NEGATIVE. Re-fetch.
 * MY PATCHSET POLLER LIED TO ME: an "Uploaded patch set N" message LISTS the votes Gerrit just
   OUTDATED, and my regex scraped `Verified-1` out of it as if live. Skip upload messages and
   truncate at "Outdated Votes:".
 * A FUNCTION-LOCAL import (`from rebar.config import load_config` inside the function) is resolved
   at CALL time — patching the module attribute silently no-ops and the test passes for the wrong
   reason. Patch `rebar.config.load_config`.
 * Store lock contention: another session was running `review-plan` on ticket 2132; `rebar comment`
   failed with `flock: could not acquire lock after 60s`. Retry.

## Open tickets from this session

 a89d task OPEN — the correctly-premised verifier successor. Carries all eight measurements so
      nobody re-derives them. Marked BRAINSTORM BEFORE DECOMPOSING: three plausible designs were
      already invalidated by measurement. Leading hypothesis is search EFFICIENCY (~32 search_files
      per criterion), not budget size.
 259c task OPEN — advisory, never-blocking plan-review nudge for a leaf with too many criteria.
      Modelled on the existing `decomp-shape` criterion. Explicitly NOT load-bearing.
 d59e task IN_PROGRESS — narrow scope landed (1064); its remaining ACs are met, close when ready.
 94b4 epic CLOSED — disproven, findings preserved on the ticket.
 65d7, 2bc7, 8070 — from the prior session, still open.
